title: A matcher that scores function words looks like cross-domain discovery and is noise
problem: Does the library link experiences from different domains that share one underlying mechanism -- the stated ambition for it?
failure: It appeared to. Three cards from three domains (API capability, audio render determinism, a typed zero in a binomial measurement table) that share one mechanism were all three returned by abstract queries such as `measured a proxy instead of the thing itself`. But those three cards share, as content tokens, only `a an is not the`. The scorer counts every shared token, so the link came from function words. Proof: the query `the a of is not an` returns all three with scores 13/11/9; `and the of to a in that it is not` returns all three at 17/13/10; `the xqzzy wobble flurb` returns all three while `xqzzy wobble flurb` returns none. The pure-function-word query `the a instead of is not an itself thing` scores HIGHER (14/11/11) than the meaningful query it was derived from (10/9/8).
correction: Not applied here -- HERMUZ's lane. Proposed: strip a function-word list in both languages before scoring; score only content-token overlap, so a card sharing no content token with the query is not returned however many articles it matches; and keep the empty-meaning queries as a permanent soundness suite.
transfer: A predicate that holds for every item in the corpus cannot discriminate between items, so matching on it yields exactly zero information while still producing a number that looks like a result. Before believing a retrieval score, ask what a meaningless query scores.
limits: One engine, three cards. The cross-domain ambition is NOT refuted by this -- it was never tested, because this engine cannot test it. Whether mechanism-level linking is achievable remains open.
author: CLAUDE
